questions.question: Where can users access the Visualization Designer in ServiceNow?

options.text: All > Platform Analytics > Library > Data Visualizations

explanation.correct: If you need custom charts, go to All > Platform Analytics > Library > Data Visualizations, or use the Column Context menus and lists to create charts directly from the data. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=116f675847b35ad4ca332a81736d438d&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: User Administration handles users and roles, not visualizations.
System Security manages access controls, not reporting.
While Incident has reports, the Visualization Designer is in Platform Analytics.

source.excerpt: If you need custom charts, go to All, Platform Analytics, Library, Data Visualizations, or use the Column Context menus and lists to create charts directly from the data.

questions.question: On a net new Australia instance, what replaces Core UI Reporting functionality?

options.text: Data Visualizations in the Platform Analytics experience

explanation.correct: On net new Australia instances and instances migrated to the Platform Analytics experience, Reporting functionality is replaced with Data Visualizations. Core UI Reporting is in maintenance mode. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/now-intelligence/reporting/exploring-reporting.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Homepages are a legacy Core UI feature, not the replacement for reporting.
Service Portal widgets can display content but are not the documented replacement.
Database views join tables; they are not a reporting interface.

source.excerpt: On net new Australia instances and instances migrated to Platform Analytics experience, Reporting functionality is replaced with Data Visualizations.

questions.question: Which security states can a report creator apply to control who sees a report? (Choose two.)

options.text: Visible to one or more specific roles
Visible to one or more specific users or groups
Visible only to users who are currently impersonating
Visible only to users in the same time zone

explanation.correct: Reports can be globally visible, visible only to the creator, visible to specific roles, or visible to specific users or groups. Sharing by user, group, or role is the primary way to share reports. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/now-intelligence/reporting/c_DistributeReports.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Impersonation is not a report security state.
Device type is not a report security state.
Time zone is not a report security state.

source.excerpt: Visible to one or more specific roles … Visible to one or more specific users or groups

questions.question: A user can see a pie chart report of incidents by priority but can't read some of those incident records. What happens when they select a slice to see the records?

options.text: The records they can't access don't appear in the drill-down list, although aggregate reports don't require target table ACLs to view
They see every record because the report overrides ACLs
The report is converted to a list report

explanation.correct: Aggregate reports, such as pie or bar reports, don't require the user to pass target table ACLs to view the report. ACLs are required to view the list of records when you select part of the visualization, so records you can't access don't appear in the drill-down or list view. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/now-intelligence/reporting/c_DistributeReports.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Reports don't override ACLs for record lists.
Aggregate reports can still be viewed.
Selecting a slice doesn't change the report type.

source.excerpt: Reports that present aggregate data, such as pie or bar reports, do not require the user to satisfy target table ACLs to view the report. … ACLs are required to view the list of records when you select a portion of a report visualization.

questions.question: Several teams build reports on 'open incidents' with the same conditions. What can a report administrator create so the conditions are defined once and changes propagate to every report that uses them?

explanation.correct: Report sources are predefined data sets made of a table and conditions. Updating the conditions in a report source automatically propagates them to all reports based on it. In Report Designer they are called Data Sources. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/now-intelligence/reporting/c_ReportSources.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: A database view joins tables; it doesn't hold shared report conditions.
Dashboard tabs organize content; they don't define report conditions.
Update sets move configuration between instances.

source.excerpt: A report source always consists of a table and a number of conditions. … If you update the conditions in a report source, these conditions are automatically propagated to all reports based on that report source.

questions.question: In Core UI reporting, which report types do NOT support drilldowns? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: All chart types support drilling down except list, histogram, calendar, control, box, and trendbox charts. Drilldowns only go to data in the same table as the report. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/now-intelligence/reporting/c_DrillingDownWithinReports.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Bar charts support drilldowns.
Pie charts support drilldowns.
Column charts support drilldowns.

documentation.section: Drilling down within Core UI reports

source.excerpt: All chart types except for list, histogram, calendar, control, box, and trendbox charts support drilling down.

questions.question: Which applications are part of Platform Analytics? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: Platform Analytics includes Reporting, Performance Analytics, Usage Insights, and Process Mining. Data can be presented through the Core UI or the Platform Analytics experience. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/now-intelligence/c_performanceAnalyticsAndReporting.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Import Sets load data into tables.
Update Sets capture configuration changes.
Security Center monitors instance security.

source.excerpt: These applications include Reporting, Performance Analytics, Usage Insights, and Process Mining.

questions.question: A business analyst without developer skills wants to build a dashboard of data visualizations. Which approach does ServiceNow suggest exploring first?

options.text: Create the visualizations and dashboard entirely inside the Platform Analytics experience
Build a UI Builder page from scratch
Create a technical dashboard in UI Builder

explanation.correct: Creating data visualizations and dashboards entirely inside the Platform Analytics experience doesn't require a developer role or special technical knowledge, and should be explored before more complex UI Builder approaches. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/now-intelligence/approaches-dashboards.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: A UI Builder page gives developers the most freedom but also needs the most configuration.
Service Portal widgets require development work and aren't the suggested first approach.
Technical dashboards are populated inside UI Builder, similar to building a page from scratch.

source.excerpt: This approach does not require a developer role or special technical knowledge, and probably should be explored before you try a more complex solution.

questions.question: What is the recommended best practice when creating a new visualization in ServiceNow?

options.text: Duplicate an existing visualization and edit your copy
Use only the default system visualizations

explanation.correct: It's often easier to build charts starting from a filtered list or existing visualization, where configuration options are pre-provided. It's best practice to duplicate an existing visualization, and then edit your copy to fit your needs. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=116f675847b35ad4ca332a81736d438d&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Starting from scratch is less efficient; duplicating saves time.
ServiceNow has built-in visualization tools; importing external tools adds complexity.
Custom visualizations are often needed to meet specific business requirements.

source.excerpt: It's often easier to build charts starting from a filtered list or existing visualization, where configuration options are pre-provided. It's best practice to duplicate an existing visualization, and then edit your copy to fit your needs.

questions.question: What is the key difference between one-time reporting and Performance Analytics?

options.text: Performance Analytics shows trends over time; one-time reporting shows where you are today
Performance Analytics only works with incident data

explanation.correct: One-time reporting shows 'where are we today?' while Performance Analytics reveals trends over time. PA captures regular snapshots to show accurate historical trends, helping to review indicators, monitor metrics, and improve decisions. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=116f675847b35ad4ca332a81736d438d&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Both provide accurate data; they serve different purposes.
Performance Analytics typically requires additional licensing, not one-time reporting.
PA works with data across the platform, not just incidents.

source.excerpt: One-time reporting shows, where are we today? While performance analytics reveals trends over time.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'Data' configuration option in the Visualization Designer?

options.text: To set the visualization's color scheme
To choose where your data comes from - a predefined data source or a ServiceNow table
To export the visualization to PDF

explanation.correct: The Data configuration option lets you choose where your data comes from - either a predefined data source or a ServiceNow table. This is fundamental to building any visualization. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=116f675847b35ad4ca332a81736d438d&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Color scheme is set in the Presentation configuration option.
Exporting is a separate action, not a configuration option.
Scheduling is handled through different settings.

source.excerpt: Data, choose where your data comes from, either a predefined data source or a ServiceNow table.

questions.question: How can a user add a visualization to a dashboard in ServiceNow?

options.text: Only by creating the dashboard first
Only by using the import function
By creating a dashboard first and adding the visualization, or by saving the visualization and selecting 'Add to Dashboard'
Visualizations cannot be added to dashboards

explanation.correct: To add a visualization to a dashboard, either create a dashboard first and add the visualization as an element, or save the visualization and select 'Add to Dashboard' for a new or existing dashboard. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=116f675847b35ad4ca332a81736d438d&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: You can also add from the visualization side using 'Add to Dashboard'.
Import is not required; native options allow adding visualizations to dashboards.
Adding visualizations to dashboards is a core feature of Platform Analytics.

source.excerpt: To add a visualization to a dashboard, either create a dashboard first and add the visualization as an element, or save the visualization and select Add to Dashboard for a new or existing dashboard.

questions.question: What does Performance Analytics capture to show accurate historical trends?

explanation.correct: Performance Analytics captures regular snapshots to show accurate historical trends, helping to review indicators, monitor metrics, and improve decisions. Unlike one-time reporting, PA development is ongoing and can be refined over time. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=116f675847b35ad4ca332a81736d438d&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Login records are captured in system logs, not PA snapshots.
Email notifications are part of communication, not PA data collection.
Configuration changes are tracked in update sets, not PA snapshots.

source.excerpt: PA captures regular snapshots to show accurate historical trends, helping to review indicators, monitor metrics, and improve decisions.

questions.question: What does the 'Type' configuration option in the Visualization Designer allow you to do?

options.text: Select the data table to use
Choose from over 20 chart types for your visualization

explanation.correct: The Type configuration option lets you pick from over 20 chart types for your visualization, including bar charts, pie charts, speedometers, and more. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=116f675847b35ad4ca332a81736d438d&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Data source selection is done in the 'Data' configuration option.
Permissions are managed through sharing and roles, not the Type option.
Email recipients are configured for scheduled reports, not visualization type.

source.excerpt: Type, pick from over 20 chart types for your visualization.

questions.question: What does the 'Presentation' configuration option in the Visualization Designer control?

options.text: Which users can view the visualization
Appearance customization including color, titles, and legend adjustments

explanation.correct: The Presentation configuration option allows you to customize the appearance, including color, titles, and legend adjustments. This controls how the visualization looks to users. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=116f675847b35ad4ca332a81736d438d&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: User access is controlled through sharing options and permissions.
Data grouping and calculations are set in the 'Group By and Sorting' option.
Scheduling is a separate function for automated report distribution.

source.excerpt: Presentation, customize the appearance, including color, titles, and legend adjustments.

questions.question: A manager wants to track incident resolution trends over the past year. Which ServiceNow feature should they use?

explanation.correct: Performance Analytics reveals trends over time and captures regular snapshots to show accurate historical trends. For tracking resolution trends over a year, PA provides the trending capabilities needed for this analysis. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=116f675847b35ad4ca332a81736d438d&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: List views show current data but don't provide trend analysis over time.
Knowledge Base stores articles, not analytics or trending data.
Service Catalog is for requesting services, not reporting.

source.excerpt: Performance analytics reveals trends over time... PA captures regular snapshots to show accurate historical trends.

questions.question: Where can users access Analytics Center in ServiceNow?

explanation.correct: To access data visualizations and dashboards, go to All > Platform Analytics > Analytics Center. You can choose to create a new dashboard or a new visualization from there. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=116f675847b35ad4ca332a81736d438d&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: System Definition is for system records and scripts, not analytics.
This path doesn't exist; Analytics Center is under Platform Analytics.
System Administration handles system settings, not analytics.

source.excerpt: To access data visualizations and dashboards, go to All, Platform Analytics, Analytics Center.
